title: Your Chief AI Officer On Demand — How the Accompaniment Works
subtitle: From readiness to a system your teams own
author: Agentik OS
abstract: This guide describes the full CAIO On Demand accompaniment — six steps from a free honest qualification call to a live, owned AI operating system. It is the document to read before your first meeting and to keep on hand as each phase delivers its work.

sections.title: What this is
sections.body: You are not buying a SaaS subscription or a consulting deck. You are engaging a senior operator who embeds with your C-suite, maps how they actually work, builds a real AI system around those people, and then transfers full ownership to your teams. Three principles govern every decision. Centralization: one dedicated server your company owns, no vendor lock-in, full export path at any time. C-Level interconnection: one function-specific dashboard per executive, all wired together so a COO metric can trigger a CFO alert in real time. Internal mastery: the engagement closes when your own people can add an agent, connect a tool, and adjust a report unaided — not when the system goes live. Every dashboard exposes its sources, logs, costs, and confidence score. There are no black boxes; every number your team sees can be traced to the event that produced it.

sections.title: How the accompaniment works
sections.body: The accompaniment runs in six sequential steps across up to five engagement phases. A free 30-minute qualification call comes first — an honest go/no-go before any money changes hands. The signed engagement then opens with discovery interviews per executive in scope (Phase 1), followed by a blueprint that maps every tool, data source, and workflow opportunity into a Company AI OS specification (Phase 1, continued). Build (Phase 2) realizes that approved blueprint into a live, client-owned system delivering value in week one. Enablement and transfer (Phases 3 and 4) onboard every audience and prove that your team can self-extend the system. Run and optimize (Phase 5) measures actual ROI by workflow cohort, monitors health, and drives the 1h/week strategic quota. The investment is €2,500 setup plus €2,500 per member per month, monthly with no minimum commitment.

sections.title: Readiness and fit (before we start)
sections.body: Before any contract is signed we run a 30-minute qualification. We assess your company across nine dimensions — executive sponsorship, tooling and API exposure, strategy and use-case clarity, data readiness, governance and compliance, culture and change appetite, AI literacy, infrastructure, and budget commitment — and score each 0 to 4. A weighted Readiness Index and a maturity tier (Nascent, Emerging, Ready, or Leading) result in one honest verdict: Go, Not yet, or Redirect. Not yet means we give you a Gap-to-Target plan and a re-qualify date at no charge. Redirect means your real need is better served by a point-SaaS, a data engineer, or an internal hire, and we name the specific alternative. We would rather lose a deal than start an engagement that is not ready to succeed. On a Go, we shape the engagement — which phases, how many members, indicative investment — and hand you a recommendation before the SOW is drafted.

sections.title: Discovery — first the work, then the tools
sections.body: We interview each executive in scope one at a time, in their professional language, with no AI jargon. The opening question is always a variant of 'walk me through your last Monday' — not 'what AI tools do you use?' People who describe their real Monday tell us everything worth knowing. We cover fourteen topics: role and responsibility, weekly and monthly rhythm, repetitive versus one-off tasks (with time and frequency), handoffs between people, tools and systems, how those tools integrate (or don't), existing automation and shadow IT, frictions, what must not be touched, improvements wanted, current and ideal states, and the gap between them. We read back a five-line summary before anything is documented. Each person's dossier is standardized so insights stack cleanly across the whole C-suite. A company rollup identifies the seams between people — the manual handoffs where automation pays best. This step is about removing the tedious parts of the job, never the person doing it.

sections.title: The blueprint — your Company AI OS
sections.body: With every discovery dossier in hand, we map the complete picture and design the system. The blueprint specifies the single centralized server including its region, stack, and export path; which C-Level micro-SaaS dashboards get built, each tied to the one job that executive does that a generic dashboard would get wrong; the inter-dashboard API contract — a typed table of which metric on one dashboard triggers which alert on another (the federation that makes this a Company AI OS and not a set of isolated screens); the six Composio connectors that map to your actual systems of record; a 30/60/90 implementation roadmap; and a projected ROI per workflow built from hours × loaded cost × frequency with every number sourced. The architecture must be reviewed and approved by your named executive sponsor before build begins. No approval, no build. This gate protects you from building the wrong thing at cost.

sections.title: Build — an operational system, not a demo
sections.body: We build exactly what the approved blueprint specified. One centralized server, client-owned from day one. One function-specific micro-SaaS per C-Level who actually exists in your org — a CFO dashboard is a finance instrument, not a repainted template. The inter-dashboard federation wired so dashboards publish and consume each other's metrics. The six Composio connectors each proven by a live data read, not an enabled checkbox. Automated reports falling out at the exact cadence your executives need — daily brief, weekly digest, monthly pack. Monitoring across five health dimensions with named thresholds and owners for each alert. Built-in instrumentation so ROI can be re-measured later against a real baseline. Each dashboard ships the moment its acceptance test passes against your real production data — not when a demo looks impressive. You see operational value in week one. Build milestones are communicated to your sponsor at every gate; no progress is ever reported that has not been verified against the live system.

sections.title: Enablement and transfer — internal mastery
sections.body: A working system that nobody uses is an expensive decoration. Phase 3 — adoption — onboards every audience at the level their role and AI literacy requires. Executives see the strategic view and their approval queue. Managers see their team's workflows and the decisions they own. Operators complete their own real task through the system, unaided, until the aha-moment lands. Internal technical owners learn the runbook, the code and configuration pointers, and the extension paths. Phase 4 — transfer — teaches three specific motions until your team performs them without us: add an agent, connect a new tool, adjust a report. Transfer is not complete when a quiz is passed or a demo is applauded. It is complete when a named member of your team does all three motions unaided, in real conditions, while we observe with our hands off the keyboard. The Autonomy-Readiness Gate documents this with objective evidence. Zero CAIO-only credentials may remain at handover. Your teams become operational guardians, not hostages.

sections.title: Run, measure and expand
sections.body: Once your team owns the system, we remain available for one deliberate hour per week. That hour is for strategy, not operations: should the support agent expand to billing? Is the CMO dashboard's data source ready for a new connector? The system running itself is the proof that the previous phases worked; the hour is the safety net without the dependency. Every quarter we produce a Quarterly Business Review: actual ROI by workflow cohort, measured against what the blueprint projected. Every figure is traceable to a telemetry event or a receipt. If a workflow's savings are decaying we surface it plainly and fix the leak before proposing a new wave. When the system is healthy and saturating its current scope, the natural expansion is the next department — the loop re-enters the blueprint phase with the advantage that the centralized server is already in place, every lesson from the first wave carried forward.

sections.title: What we need from you
sections.body: Three things make the engagement succeed before the first day of work. First, a named sponsor: one executive with the authority to approve the architecture and attend the milestone demos. Without a sponsor the engagement cannot gate-pass into build. Second, the three-reports tip: before our qualification call, ask each C-Level in scope to name the three reports they look at most often and estimate how many hours per week their team spends producing them. Those answers are the fastest path to the highest-value automations. Third, honest access: tools your teams actually use, even the informal ones; any existing reporting or automation flows, however scrappy; a candid sense of where the most repetitive work sits today. We handle the rest — permissions, integrations, documentation, and the system itself. To start, book the free 30-minute qualification call. We will tell you honestly whether this engagement fits before either party commits a euro.
